stem: An adult with type 1 diabetes uses rapid-acting insulin with meals and an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio (ICR). Which statement by the client shows correct understanding?

options.A: I estimate the carbohydrate in the meal and use my prescribed ICR to help determine the mealtime insulin dose; I may also need individualized guidance for fat, protein, current glucose, trends, activity, or illness.
options.B: I should give the same mealtime insulin dose every day even when the carbohydrate amount changes substantially.
options.C: Carbohydrate content should be ignored when calculating mealtime insulin because only the fasting glucose determines the dose.
options.D: Using an ICR means I should avoid carbohydrate-containing foods rather than match insulin to the meal.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend teaching most adults with type 1 diabetes to match mealtime insulin to carbohydrate intake and, when relevant, the glycemic effects of fat and protein. Current insulin plans commonly use an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio for prandial dosing, with additional adjustment based on concurrent glucose, trends, physical activity, illness, and other individualized factors. B and C disconnect mealtime insulin from nutritional needs. D misrepresents carbohydrate counting as carbohydrate avoidance.
educational_objective: Use an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio to match prandial insulin to meal carbohydrate while incorporating other person-specific factors that can change mealtime insulin needs.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Section 9 Recommendation 9.3 and insulin-treatment tables — educate most adults with type 1 diabetes to match mealtime insulin to carbohydrate intake and, depending on needs/preferences, fat and protein; mealtime/correction insulin may be based on ICR, ISF, target glucose, and trends. Section 5 Recommendation 5.27 and nutrition text — insulin-to-carbohydrate ratios can assist meal-to-meal insulin adjustment
source_claim_supported: For adults with type 1 diabetes using flexible prandial insulin, carbohydrate counting and an individualized ICR can guide mealtime insulin dosing, with other meal and clinical factors incorporated as needed.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; calculate, administer, and teach individualized insulin therapy safely
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — carbohydrate counting and prandial insulin matching
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source recall item into medication-management teaching and corrected the client-need category from Basic Care and Comfort to Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies. The final version also updates the older carbohydrate-only framing by preserving current ADA guidance that fat, protein, glucose trends, activity, and illness can modify individualized prandial dosing.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: type 1 diabetes / carbohydrate counting / prandial insulin
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Sections 9 and 5. ICR-based mealtime dosing and individualized adjustment for meal composition and clinical factors are directly supported.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A preserves the ICR construct without claiming carbohydrate is the only determinant of prandial insulin. No universal ICR value or dose formula is invented.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it matches flexible prandial insulin to carbohydrate and acknowledges other individualized modifiers.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; fixed dosing despite large carbohydrate changes can mismatch insulin to meal exposure.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; carbohydrate intake is a major prandial-dosing consideration.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; carbohydrate counting supports matching, not compulsory carbohydrate avoidance.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects the current individualized prandial-insulin framework.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern meal-related insulin decisions rather than unrelated nutrition facts.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies is the correct category because the core task is insulin-dose education and adjustment.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked ICR terminology, carbohydrate-counting role, fat/protein nuance, correction factors, activity/illness modifiers, fixed-regimen distinction, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
